timeline.change: Suzuki buys the HopeStar ON360 design from Hope Motor Company
April: Jimny LJ10 launches, 359 cc air-cooled two-stroke twin, 25 PS; first series-production kei 4x4
May: LJ20 with water-cooled L50 twin (28 PS), vertical grille, steel-roof van
September: LJ50 539 cc three-cylinder two-stroke for export (33 PS)
June: Jimny 55 (SJ10) in Japan; NZ assembly of the LJ50 begins late in the year
Jimny 8 / LJ80: 797 cc F8A four-stroke, 41 PS, wider track, taller gearing
Metal doors available; LJ81 pickup on a 2,200 mm wheelbase

identify.intro: Engines, grilles and bodies were swapped over five decades, so check what you're actually looking at.

items.head: Engine
items.body: LJ10: air-cooled 359 cc twin. LJ20: water-cooled 359 cc twin. LJ50/SJ10: 539 cc three-cylinder two-stroke. LJ80/SJ20: 797 cc four-stroke four.

items.head: Grille
items.body: The LJ10 has horizontal slots; Suzuki says the LJ20's vertical eight-slot grille became the Jimny's signature face.

items.head: Spare wheel
items.body: Japanese kei trucks kept the spare inside to stay under 3 m; export trucks and the LJ20F carried it outside.

values.intro: LJs are rare in the US; restored LJ20s and early Jimnys bring the most.
